subject: Re: Q1 pricing experiments — GM impact, forecast updates, and backfill assumptions
thread_body:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Q1 pricing experiments — GM impact + forecast updates (need backfill assumptions)

Laura,

I’m updating the Feb–Apr forecast and trying to land the GM impact of the Q1 pricing tests, but I’m stuck on two assumptions:

1) How we expect the streaming disconnect + rounding fixes/backfills to flow through (timing + magnitude)
2) Whether we’re treating any customer make-goods (credits) as a one-time COGS/contra-rev adjustment vs ongoing unit economics

Can you confirm what Finance wants for the forecast version that goes out Monday?

Working doc (sensitivity scenarios):
- Unit economics sensitivity: token cost vs price (Drive) — google_drive://shared_drives/finance-and-legal/unit-economics-sensitivity-token-cost-vs-price

Questions I need answered to finalize:
- Backfill: do we expect any net reduction to billed tokens for Jan/Feb (i.e., invoice deltas), or is this just a console alignment fix?
- If invoice deltas: do we book impact in the month of the original usage (true-up), or in the month the credit/refund is issued?
- Experiments: are we okay assuming the free-credit structure test increases paid conversion but reduces GM short-term due to higher credit burn? I can run both ways but need a default.

Thanks,
Rishi

—
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A, Redwood Inference



From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Q1 pricing experiments — GM impact + forecast updates (need backfill assumptions)

Rishi,

Default for Monday forecast:
- Assume NO broad-based invoice reduction from the fixes (i.e., not a “rate cut”).
- Assume targeted credits for confirmed metering defects only, booked when issued.

We should not “restate” Jan usage in the forecast model until Engineering confirms invoice impact is material and systematic.

Emily is tracking known cases and expected exposure. We’ll also need Ethan to confirm whether the backfill changes billing aggregates or just reporting/console.

Laura



From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 10:29 AM
Subject: Re: Q1 pricing experiments — GM impact + forecast updates (need backfill assumptions)

Adding what I have so far:

- We have 3 confirmed “billing-impacting defect” buckets under review:
  (a) streaming disconnect accounting (possible overbilling on partial streams)
  (b) invoice aggregator rounding mismatch (per-request rounding behavior)
  (c) retries double-counted on one endpoint (still triaging scope)

- Engineering is planning a backfill window (TBD, likely a targeted range vs all history). The expectation is most accounts are within tolerance; any refunds/credits will be case-by-case.

- For forecast, I’d follow Laura’s guidance: model a small reserve line for one-time credits, not a shift in unit economics. I can send you the latest reconciliation summary once it’s updated.

Reference:
- Feb sample reconciliation (Drive): google_drive://shared_drives/finance-and-legal/meter-reconciliation-results-sample-b-2026-02

Emily

—
Emily Stone
Billing Controls, Redwood Inference



From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 12:11 PM
Subject: Re: Q1 pricing experiments — GM impact + forecast updates (need backfill assumptions)

Quick engineering view (still validating):

- Streaming disconnect fix (PR 41903) is billing-impacting for a subset of streaming requests where we were attributing tokens after client disconnect. Correct behavior: do not bill tokens generated after disconnect; bill what was actually streamed.
  - PR: github://redwood/pr_41903

- Rounding fix (PR 41888) changes invoice aggregation logic to match ADR: no per-request rounding; round at aggregation window / invoice level. That can move totals up/down slightly depending on traffic shape.
  - PR: github://redwood/pr_41888

- Backfill plan (ENG-4826) is to regenerate billing aggregates for a targeted window and compare deltas before/after. We don’t expect large systematic reductions, but there will be some corrections. If we find an outlier account (or cohort), we’ll flag Finance before touching invoices.
  - Linear: linear://ENG-4826

For Monday forecast, I’d assume “immaterial overall; localized credits where needed.” I can provide an upper-bound estimate once we finish the dry-run diff.

Ethan

—
Ethan Park
Platform Control Plane, Redwood Inference



From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 1:07 PM
Subject: Re: Q1 pricing experiments — GM impact + forecast updates (need backfill assumptions)

Thanks Ethan — this helps.

Two follow-ups for forecast + board narrative:

1) Can you give me a rough “ceiling” on exposure for the targeted backfill window? Even a wide band (e.g., <0.5% of Hosted revenue for the month) is enough for my model + risk language.

2) For the rounding change specifically: if rounding at invoice-level can go either direction, are we expecting net neutral across the population? Or is there a bias (e.g., high-cardinality small requests leading to consistent downward adjustment)?

I’ll proceed with:
- No change to steady-state token economics
- A one-time credit reserve line for Q1 tied to defect remediation

Rishi



From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 9:36 AM
Subject: Re: Q1 pricing experiments — GM impact + forecast updates (need backfill assumptions)

Rishi,

Preliminary ceiling (NOT final, but directionally useful):

- Streaming disconnect correction: if we assume worst-case on the affected window, upper bound is low single-digit % of streaming usage, but streaming is only a subset of Hosted. Translating to revenue exposure, we believe it’s <1% of Hosted revenue for the month, likely materially less.

- Rounding: should be close to net neutral across the population. It can swing either direction; bias depends on distribution of small requests. For typical traffic, the effect is very small (think basis points), but we saw a few accounts with higher variance due to very high request counts with small token totals.

We’ll send Finance the dry-run diff summary before any actual backfill run.

Ethan



From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: Q1 pricing experiments — GM impact + forecast updates (need backfill assumptions)

Rishi,

Use Ethan’s bound (<1% Hosted revenue monthly; likely less) and describe it as “billing control remediation / one-time customer credits” rather than structural margin change.

On experiments:
- Yes, assume the revised free-credit structure can depress GM short-term via higher credit burn. We should separate “promo/credits” effects from “price realization” in the narrative.
- Please include a footnote that reported GM will be noisy until the backfill window closes and we’ve issued any credits.

Emily will keep you posted on actual issued credits so you can true-up the forecast line.

Laura

—
Laura Bennett
VP Finance (Exec Sponsor)
Redwood Inference
